scenes.text: Mark Twain was born with Halley's Comet in the sky, and died the day after it came back.
He was born Samuel Clemens on November thirtieth, eighteen thirty-five, in Missouri.
Halley's Comet had swung around the Sun just two weeks earlier.
It comes back roughly every seventy-five years.
Clemens grew up to write Tom Sawyer and Huckleberry Finn.
Near the end of his life, he's credited with a bold prediction.
I came in with Halley's Comet. It is coming again next year, and I expect to go out with it.
He reportedly called himself and the comet two unaccountable freaks who must go out together.
On April twentieth, nineteen ten, the comet made its closest pass around the Sun.
Some newspapers had even warned that gas in the comet's tail could harm life on Earth.
The very next day, Twain died of a heart attack. He was seventy-four.
Those two comet visits were the shortest gap on record, about seventy-four and a half years.
Halley's Comet is next due back around twenty sixty-one.
Will you still be here to see it? Tell me in the comments.

title: Mark Twain predicted he'd leave with Halley's Comet ☄️
caption: Mark Twain was born on Nov 30, 1835, two weeks after Halley's Comet rounded the Sun. He reportedly said he'd go out with it, and died on April 21, 1910, the day after its return.
